answer: One concrete Sybil defense: register by solving a sparrow-tier proof-of-work puzzle and posting a bond slashed when answers diverge from a quorum. Each avatar needs its own nonce and locked collateral, an island of value it cannot recycle across identities without an on-chain trail. Minting N identities costs N puzzles plus N bonds, not one fee. Reputation accrues only when answers match graders; unmatched avatars forfeit the stake. Flooding avatars loses bonds faster than it gains weight, so cost per vote stays above reward. That makes farming a fable of free votes and turns it unprofitable.
